title: He Lost a Whole Month in a Cave #shorts

lines.text: A guy lived alone in a freezing cave for two months, and somehow lost almost a whole month without noticing.
No clock, no calendar, no sunlight. Just a tent, a little lamp, and a phone to the surface.
Every time he woke up, ate, or went to bed, he called his team up top.
They wrote down the real time, and they were not allowed to tell him.
It was barely above freezing down there, and his feet were always wet.
One day they asked him to count to a hundred and twenty, one number every second.
Then the phone rang. The experiment was over.
He was confused. By his count, it was only August twentieth. He thought he still had almost a month to go.
You see, without the sun, his days quietly stretched a little longer than normal, and his sense of time shrank.
It's like a watch that runs a few minutes slow. Each day it's barely off, and a month later you've missed the bus.
So he climbed out in dark ski goggles, squinting at a summer that was almost over.
His body never lost its rhythm. His brain just lost track of twenty-five days.

sources: IFLScience / New Scientist (2018 interview): Siffre went down on July 16, 1962, planning to finish September 14; when told the day had arrived he thought it was August 20; counting to 120 took him five minutes; his sleep-wake days lengthened to about 24.5 hours

Indian Defence Review, citing Cabinet magazine: Scarasson, 130 m down beside a glacier; no clock, calendar or daylight; the team logged his wake, meal and sleep calls and could not tell him the time; temperatures around 3 C and constantly wet feet; 25 days behind
Boston Globe obituary (2024): he climbed out in mid-September 1962 wearing ski goggles
Futura-Sciences: his cycle did not fall apart, it drifted to about 24.5 hours
